provenance.notes: ruleSetGroups and checks are extracted mechanically. `gaps` states what the extracted rules do not contain; each status is backed by a value in `checks` or by the rule text itself. Rule text is kept exactly as CLDR ships it, including forms a reviewer may consider errors.

format.description: CLDR rule-based number format (RBNF) rule sets, parsed. Rule selection and substitution semantics are those of UTS #35 part 3, Rule-Based Number Formatting; tools/extract/language/rbnf.mjs holds a reference interpreter for the constructs used here.

ruleKinds.base: applies from baseValue up to the next rule
ruleKinds.fraction: descriptor x.x (number with a fractional part)

tokenKinds.quotient: <…< : format floor(n / divisor) with the named rule set (or the current one)
tokenKinds.remainder: >…> : format n mod divisor with the named rule set (or the current one); for fraction rules, the fractional digits one by one; for the negative rule, the absolute value
tokenKinds.same: =…= : format n itself with the named rule set or the given DecimalFormat pattern
tokenKinds.optional: […] : emitted only when n is not a multiple of divisor

gaps.need: Amount in words on cheques and invoices names the currency and its subunit with number agreement (singular, dual, plural 3–10, accusative singular 11–99, singular after hundreds/thousands) and joins major and minor amounts.
gaps.status: RBNF has no currency rule set for ar (checks.containsCurrencyRuleSet is false). The counted noun and its forms must come from the currency layer (CLDR currencies.json displayName-count-*), not from here.

gaps.need: The closing phrase «فقط لا غير» (and the optional opening «فقط») that Arabic cheques and invoices put around the amount.
gaps.status: Absent from RBNF (checks.containsOnlyPhrase is false). No CLDR source; needs an authored, reviewed string.

gaps.need: The dual of the counted noun replaces the numeral two (ريالان / ريالين), and 2000 / 2 000 000 use dual forms in the case the sentence requires.
gaps.status: RBNF emits bare numerals only. It writes 2000 as «ألفين» in %spellout-numbering and «ألفي» in the cardinal rule sets, and has no rule for a construct-state or case choice.

gaps.need: Case endings: nominative/accusative-genitive forms of tens and duals (عشرون / عشرين, مائتان / مائتين) and tanween on the counted noun after 11–99 (ريالًا).
gaps.status: RBNF contains no tashkeel at all (checks.containsAnyTashkeel is false) and only nominative tens and hundreds.

gaps.need: Numerals 3–10 take the opposite gender of the counted noun; 11–19 have masculine and feminine compound forms.
gaps.status: In CLDR 49 %spellout-cardinal-feminine uses the same words as the masculine set for 3–10 and builds 13–19 from %spellout-numbering; the words differ between the two sets only at 1, 2 and 12. Recorded as found, not corrected.

gaps.need: Minor units are read as a whole number of subunits (… وخمسون قرشًا), never digit by digit.
gaps.status: The x.x rule reads fractional digits one by one after «فاصل»; an amount-in-words implementation must split major and minor units before calling the rules.
Rule sets fall back to the pattern #,##0 from 10^18.
